findings.initial_issue: Pre-dispatch cancellation/known rollback could leave permanent commit or hash-bearing upload markers, eventually consuming the finite protection capacity.
findings.resolution: Upload binding becomes admitted only after BeginTransaction confirms. Positively pre-admission failures may release upload protection. Admitted transactions release markers only after the actual retirement join observes TransactionOutcome.RolledBack; Unknown and rollback-unconfirmed records remain protected.
findings.title: Known non-admission or rollback must retire recovery protection

findings.initial_issue: Collection enumerated final manifests but did not reclaim interrupted .json.new writes or old unmanifested .part files.
findings.resolution: Old inactive orphan parts and temporary manifests are eligible after the configured grace period. The unmanifested-part cleanup skips parts with a final manifest; ordinary manifest processing still applies, and complete hash-bearing uncertain manifests continue to protect blobs. Reference checks still precede immutable-blob deletion.
findings.title: Abandoned staging temporaries need grace collection

findings.initial_issue: Direct writes to final recovery JSON could publish malformed records after interruption; the caller enrolled cleanup only after ProtectCommit returned.
findings.resolution: ProtectCommit writes and flushes .json.new, atomically moves it to the final identity, then fsyncs the directory before COMMIT. The caller enrolls protection before that call. Confirmed rollback removes complete/temporary records; old unpublished recovery temporaries receive grace cleanup. Complete uncertain records remain protected.
findings.title: Commit recovery records must publish atomically before dispatch

findings.initial_issue: Repeated oldest-100 scans could revisit the same protected/undelivered records forever and never reach later eligible operations or confirmed recovery records.
findings.resolution: Bounded per-phase cursors persist in atomic maintenance.json and wrap on a short/empty page. Database scan positions advance only after confirmed commit. Protected entries are revisited on subsequent sweeps without blocking later work. The disk admission reserves 8 KiB for complete plus temporary progress metadata.
findings.title: Protected oldest rows must not starve later maintenance work

findings.initial_issue: An unowned post-native-retirement filesystem continuation could be dropped by process exit after a DataSource join, leaving a known-rollback marker unrecoverable from absence alone.
findings.resolution: Thirty-two application protection slots are reserved before mutation DB admission and retained through native plus filesystem obligations. Completed tasks are removed. After handlers stop, the top-level finally joins sources and owned application cleanup on normal and exceptional exits before releasing owner.lock. HTTP paths retain their finite 100 ms session closure and do not retain RequestContext or DI scope.
findings.title: Application retirement continuations need bounded ownership and a shutdown join

findings.initial_issue: EnumerateFiles followed by FileInfo.Length could race an unsynchronized rename/deletion and fail an unrelated create/upload with FileNotFoundException.
findings.resolution: Metadata publication/removal is synchronized with quota observation. The scan tolerates files already removed, while full active reservations conservatively cover not-yet-written upload bytes and metadata. It does not drop arbitrary I/O failures or weaken the disk bound.
findings.title: Quota scans must tolerate normal concurrent temporary-file retirement

limits: This is source approval plus review of focused Linux regression evidence, not final acceptance of the in-progress complete B21 package matrix.
B22 crash/fault/30-minute/24-hour/72-hour evidence, B23 performance comparison and B24 final domain release are not established here.
Other platforms and power-loss durability are not accepted. The filesystem profile has one process owner and offline maintenance.
Seven-day replay is not permanent duplicate prevention. Missing durable records do not establish rollback; complete unresolved recovery remains protected.
Outbox publication has a 15-second admission token and the existing separate 30-second consumer COMMIT deadline; no <=15-second shutdown promise.
positive_checks: Authenticated tenant/principal/semantic idempotency scope; fixed canonical v1 request framing; exact durable response replay.
PostgreSQL DO NOTHING RETURNING followed by typed FindAsync; SQLite Immediate transactions; result/business/outbox atomicity.
Tenant-filtered keyset with unique tie-breaker and authenticated cursor; protected operation recovery; attachment reference authorization and expected-version CAS.
Bounded outbox claim/lease/attempts; claim transaction ends before publication; stable event identity and persistent consumer deduplication; stale acknowledgments use attempt CAS.
32 KiB streamed attachment writes and reads, whole-upload reservation, durable blob before reference, active/uncertain manifest protection and reference-aware grace collection.
Finite HTTP session close, independent bounded application retirement ownership, no ended RequestContext/DI retention, truthful top-level shutdown join.
Canonical executable and compiled samples use PackageReference; static application metadata/JSON; no new managed database/server substitute or public/native ABI.

Recognize at most one exact bounded SQLx 0.9.0 ColumnResolver catalog query before the next business operations SELECT; record statement SHA-256 and count, skip no other SQL.
